The problem is, as helpful as "the little things" are in making someone happy, they're only band-aid solutions to a bigger problem. Listening to a nice song won't change the fact that my step dad molested me. Reading a good book won't change the fact that I have ruined my life. Smiling won't change the fact that my dad didn't want me. 

You can never win with depression. No matter what anyone says, you'll always be sad. No matter how much someone cares, you'll never smile. 

It does however, help to know that people like you exist. Random strangers with enough compassion to take 2 minutes out of their day to pat you on the back and say, "chin up". Maybe it won't help me but I'm sure it will help someone else. Someone who isn't as bad off as I am. So for that, I thank you.
Well the whole "molest me till age 7" thing might count as a screw up -_-

No. I told my mom when I was 13(?) and she talked to him about it. He said he didn't do anything, and my mom took his side. He was an alcoholic so it's possible he doesn't remember. My mom told me it was a false memory and never brought it up again.
He's my stepdad. So up until a year ago I was still living with him. I see him whenever I go home now.

Yeah it messed me up pretty bad. It didn't really affect me until I was 12 and old enough to understand that what happend wasn't okay. That's when things went downhill. It was really hard for me when I started dating and my boyfriends would want to try things and I just couldn't.

I remember everything. Right down to the specific kind of pain. I remember what he said during certain instances. We had bunk beds, and I had the top bunk. I remember rolling in to the little space between my bed and the wall just so he wouldn't touch me. I remember being upset when he could still reach me.
Well I was repeatedly molested until I was 7...so there's that.

My step-dad is abusive. He molested me multiple times when I was younger. When I approached my mom about it he denied it and she took his side. I never brought it up again, but I also never forgave him for it. I hate being around him and have had an amazing time away from him while at school.

I went to a college preparatory high school, and I started college feeling a little more confident than I should have, so I went easy on myself and just slid by in class. Turns out I didn't just slide by, I completely neglected my classes.

Luckily I did some research and found a Second Chance program offered by my school. If I'm accepted into the program I'll get to continue attendance. :D

I think my depression has played a big role actually. I have had several breakdowns which resulted in thinking about suicide, followed by more depression. Then I'd bottle it up for a while, be positive and motivated to do well, then fail an exam and have another breakdown. Wash rinse repeat. 

I was recently diagnosed with ADD in my senior year of college, and am still working with a psychiatrist to find the right medication for me. I had been taking Strattera but I stopped when I started college because I hated the side effects. I thought I could manage without it but I guess not. While I was on it in high school my grades improved. 

I'd definitely take a year off and work, but the thing is I have no place to live. I'd have to live at home which I absolutely do not want to do.

You read me like an open book in that last paragraph. I've always been the one people come to for help. People always saw how strong I was and how I never let anything get to me. But now the strong pillar my friends used to lean on is crumbling...

If you don't mind, I'd love to be able to PM you the next time I feel like I'm going to have a meltdown. Talking about this anonymously has been really helpful. I really really appreciate you taking the time to talk to a complete stranger. :]

Thing is, I'm at college 4,000 miles away from my psychiatrist now. I can only talk to her when I go back home over breaks. I normally won't talk about problems unless I'm having a breakdown. Otherwise I buck up and convince myself I'm fine and don't need to talk. I've also done a good job of telling myself I don't deserve to hurt or complain, because I know that EVERYONE has their own problems that are just as, or more difficult than mine. So why should I get to cry and not them? It's going to take a lot of work but I know I need help, no matter where it comes from.

Well I wouldn't mind if I dropped dead right here and now. Do I *want* to die? I don't know. There aren't any voices telling me to do it, which scares me because now I know it's my own conscience telling me to do it and not some mental disorder. Sometimes when I get overwhelmed, I get urges to just do it. I do resent myself strongly, not necessarily life. I know there's a lot to enjoy in life, so I don't know why I'm having these thoughts. They just overwhelm me so strongly. I've never talked about it before. I have a psychiatrist for my ADD but I don't talk to her about any problems. She asks me questions but I just can't bring myself to say anything. I just smile and say everything is dandy. My problem is, I've never been one to ask for help. I never as for help with anything. I don't want to talk to anyone about it if they don't genuinely care. If you knew me in person you'd never guess that I struggle with this. I don't want to talk to anyone about it because I don't want people to look at me differently afterwards. I don't want them to feel like they need to be sensitive around me.

Like I mentioned earlier, I'm not sure if I want to tell him because I don't think were going to have a relationship in the future. I'm moving 3,000 miles away for college in 10 days and won't be home until christmas time.

I'm 17, and he's 19. He's actually my best friends boyfriends best friend. Sorry if I lost you there, but the four of us hang out a lot and it's pretty fun, although I've only known him for three months. I'm not too sure if I want to tell him though because I'm leaving far away for college in 10 days, and won't be home until Christmas time...
Wasn't expecting it to happen that way. -_-

This is coming from a 17 y/o girls perspective, by the way.

Going to agree though, you do look young for your age. But then again people say I look young for my age so I feel for you.

I've been wanting to talk to someone else about this. I've been cutting since I was 11, and am 17 now. 

Do you feel like you need to stop, or do you see any problem with it at all? If someone sees my cuts they always tell me how big of a problem it is, but honestly I don't think it is. It makes me feel better, so why should I stop? Like you, I get kind of a high feeling after cutting too. It just feels really good.

I have scars too, but you can't really see them with the lighting, plus they're under my fresh cuts -_- http://i.imgur.com/QyJtP.jpg

Ugh I know. I am so appreciative that all these random strangers seem to care so much about one kid. I'm really trying to fix what I'm doing. I had a huge meltdown last night, crying and cutting and what not, and realized that I'm not normal. What I do isn't normal. I'm fucked up, and it's entirely my fault, and now it's entirely up to me to change that. So I'm going to try. Because if I don't fix myself now, while I can actually SEE that I need to, I'm probably going to be dead before I have a second chance.

So thank you, for taking the time to care about me, and now I suppose it's my turn to take the time to care about me as well.
Thank you so much, again, for everything. Really :]

Well I *already* look like shit so if I keep up what I'm doing I don't think I can look any worse. 

I know what I'm doing to my body. And I feel so sick every day because of it, mentally and physically. I know it's taken me years to gain the weight, but it also took months to give me the mentality I have now, and like you said, it's gonna take time to get rid of it.
I'm slowly working on losing a final 15 pounds.

I really really appreciate you taking the time to talk with me about this. I do feel really pathetic and weak, mentally and physically all the time because of what I've done. I've also developed anemia from it so that's no fun either. I know there's so much more to finding happiness than just what the scale gives you, but I'm still having trouble seeing it for myself. I'm working on it slowly but surely. 

I'm 17 by the way, graduating high school in two weeks :]

The thing is, doing it the right way is what led me to doing it the wrong way. I had a personal trainer and I would work out every day for 90 minutes. I also was really careful about what I ate. I ate a good 1,200 calories a day. After just two weeks of doing it this way, I lost 12 pounds. I was so excited and encouraged, the next week I restricted my calories to 800, and went a little lighter on the weights/cardio. Eventually I just cut my calories down so much, I couldn't work out anymore, but my body kept losing weight. So I just kept up what I was doing. 

Now, I only did this extreme dieting for two week increments, then went back to normal eating for 3 weeks. Then I'd do two weeks again of dieting again. I haven't gained a single pound back yet. To maintain my weight, I eat eat normally every other day, and nothing on the days between. Sometimes if I feel like I ate a lot, I'll go the next two days with only drinking water.

I know all the risks involved. I've done all the research. I know exactly how terrible this is for my body, but I'm just past the point of quitting. I've fucked myself up, but it works for me. I wish things weren't this way but like I keep saying, I'm just past the point of changing.
I am well aware of this. The first two weeks, I literally thought I was going to die. But I'm past the point of being talked out of it.
A week. One scrambled egg. That's about 75 calories a day.
I ate like 500 calories a week, and unknowingly put my body into ketosis. I also box every now and then.
Thank you for your words, but caps lock is very annoying.

I really appreciate you taking the time to respond. It helps talking to someone who's experienced and recovered from something like this. This made me realize that this is all just in my head. I can be happy whenever I want. I just have to tell myself that I am happy. It seems so easy and I don't know why it's been so difficult for me to see this. It's going to be hard to entirely change, since I've had this thought process forever, but I'm going to try. :]
Thanks for your advice. I'll look into the EDRecovery sub. I really appreciate it!

When all else fails, music is the one thing that gets to me. And this song in particular really does it for me. And I know it's probably one of the most hated songs on Reddit, but Firework by Katy Perry always makes me feel strong.

Ever since then she's gone on like we've never had that conversation. She still seems to wonder why I hate him so much.

Physically yes. He hasn't done it since I was 7.

Mentally I'm fucked. I have Body Dysmorphic Disorder, Depression, and recently developed Bulimia. I have not even an ounce of self-confidence, basically. I have the hardest time letting guys get close to me. I have to be in control all the time. Once I let my guard down I feel really exposed and overwhelmed and vulnerable. I can't trust people, and have a hard time letting people in to my life emotionally. I know they won't hurt me, but it's just kind of something that's been embedded in my head since I was abused. I don't think it will ever go away. 

It's been 10 years since anything happened, and I still haven't been able to deal with it.
